- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward price spikes; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after strong upward moves, underestimating subsequent rebounds.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the middle of the 30-day window, especially when true prices are trending higher.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves near the end of the 30-day window, often missing the final 3–5 days of decline.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late to capture the true trend reversal.
